title: Interrupting large uploads leads to re-upload as additional files aren't considered for snapshots
body:
Output of `restic version`
--------------------------
restic 0.17.3 compiled with go1.23.3 on linux/amd64


What backend/service did you use to store the repository?
---------------------------------------------------------
local


Problem description / Steps to reproduce
----------------------------------------
I am backing up a local repository containing 700,000 files and 16TB of data. 

The backup process has been interrupted multiple times with CTRL+C after running for over 30 minutes. 
> signal interrupt received, cleaning up
> Fatal: unable to save snapshot: context canceled
> 2025/03/21 11:44:13 backup on profile 'default': exit status 1

Each time the backup was interrupted, the number of "additional files" reported by Restic increased. 
> 11173 additional files were found in the repo, which likely contain duplicate data.

These additional files existed in the repository but were not included in any snapshot. 
Running the recovery process did not incorporate them into a snapshot either. 
Allowing the backup to continue until completion also failed to include these files in the final snapshot. 
This suggests that they were processed again, meaning they would have been uploaded again if it had been a remote repository. 
Consequently, it appears that safely interrupting Restic during large uploads is not feasible, especially considering my repository will take eight days to upload. 
Therefore, the only reliable methods for uploading a large repository seems to be "exclude-larger-than" or to upload one large folder at a time until a safe snapshot is created.
Which seems to mean I would have to break down the 8 day upload into 4-8h chunks each time adjusting the "larger then" or "which folders".


Expected behavior
-----------------
Graceful handling of interruption and the additional files get added to the final snapshot and don't get uploaded again
Recover includes the additional files into a snapshot #5287 
Maybe there could be a temporary _inprogress snapshot and every 10 minutes uploads get committed to it and once they get put into a real snapshot they are removed from the _inprogress snapshot

<!--
Describe what you'd like restic to do differently.
-->

Actual behavior
---------------
It very much looks like the files get uploaded again and I need to run prune to just remove them and the upload time is wasted

In this section, please try to concentrate on observations, so only describe
what you observed directly.
-->

Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------
Because restic isn't resuming gracefully after being interrupted

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant4  you had mentioned that the additional files would be included in my final snapshot once the backup completes. looks from the log files above like this isn't the case

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Your successful full backup says:

```
Files:           0 new,     0 changed, 572702 unmodified
Dirs:            0 new,  2381 changed,  9698 unmodified
Added to the repository: 225.781 KiB (111.122 KiB stored)
```

So clearly it is not re-uploading the files, it is reusing the data uploaded in previous failed jobs, as designed.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hm the backup was run multiple times and this is just the last time with close to 0 modifications in the source folder. I shared it to show that even though the backup completed the additional files are still there.

> So clearly it is not re-uploading the files, it is reusing the data uploaded in previous failed jobs, as designed.
So I can't see how this proves that nothing was re-uploaded.

My assumption is. 
- If the "additional files" are my uploaded files where the backup didn't complete 
- then they would end up in the snapshot when the backup does complete. 
- and they would be removed from being additional files as they are now in a snapshot

Is that assumption correct? And if yes why are the additional files still there when they are now inside the last snapshot?

My only conclusion is that the additional files are being ignore and are re-processed. 
I'm open to being wrong here but I would like to see how we can be certain  that the code works as intended

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Did the data change between backups? Did you edit the source paths / command sources at all?

You mentioned that the interruptions were every 30 minutes but we can't see from your output how much of that time was spent scanning source data etc. If it took 20 minutes to rescan the source, calculating new data to send etc., perhaps restic only had 10 minutes per run to actually send new data.

It might help in the future to test and provide output of your commands using restic, rather than a third party tool, as we cannot see what parameters are being passed to restic and it introduces an unknown element.

"Additional files" in this context do not refer to your individual files but refer to pack files stored in the repository. The data that is inside these packs is included in the backup now that it has completed, but perhaps they contain data which was only completely deduplicated on the final run - that is to say they may contain duplicate data which is no longer needed; particularly since you're backing up several TB of data. Restic does not remove any packs unless a `prune` is run so it is to be expected that these additional files are not automatically removed, assuming that the process is working and they do contain data that's no longer needed.

To be sure that this is a bug it would be helpful to have reproduceable steps, using only restic, and output from each attempt, with checks on the size of the repository between each run. Obviously not with TBs of data though :-)

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
During a backup restic periodically uploads new index files. Currently this happens each ten minutes or after uploading 50GB data (happens earlier for small files). A later backup run will reuse blobs that are included in the index. If you interrupt a backup, you can run `restic repair index` to also index pack files that have been uploaded between the index uploads.

Other than that, you're looking for https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/2280 . Is there anything left to discuss here?

Thank you for the explanation, Michael!  I have two suggestions:

1. upload index files on SIGINT/SIGTERM (ah, this is #2367) *and/or*

Something like:

> 11173 additional files were found in the repo, which likely contain duplicate data.
> This is non-critical, you can run `restic prune` to remove unreferenced files or
> `restic repair index` to incorporate them into the index.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
For now the only two options are `restic repair index` (which adds those files to the index) or `restic prune` (which deletes them). Both solve the problem and work fine.

Preferring `prune` over `repair index` is primarily my personal preference, simply because `prune` is the standard command to remove unnecessary data from a repository. In contrast, `repair index` is intended for fixing a damaged repository and is likely used a lot less than `prune`.
